device.category: monophonic analogue synthesizer, semi-modular, desktop / Eurorack
device.based_on: RSF Kobol Expander (France, late 1970s). The Behringer guide never names it; the panel layout, the morphing oscillator waveforms and the per-oscillator VCAs are the Kobol's.

sources.title: KOBOL EXPANDER Quick Start Guide
sources.note: 66 numbered controls with one-line descriptions, a Hints and Tips box, a getting-started page and a specifications table. English controls are on pages 26 to 28. No CC map, no envelope times.

sources.title: Kobol Expander front panel image
sources.note: Used for control ranges printed on the panel (VCO 10 Hz to 10 kHz, VCF 16 Hz to 16 kHz, voltage processor gains 0 to 2), the signal-flow lines, and the LED colours.

architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic; poly chain across multiple units through the SynthTRIBE app
architecture.summary: Two VCOs, each with a waveform control that morphs continuously from triangle through ramp and sawtooth to square and pulse, with pulse width modulation from the LFO, the filter envelope or both at the pulse end. Each VCO has its own VCA for level, and both feed a 24 dB/octave low-pass filter that self-oscillates. A second VCA shaped by its own ADS envelope follows the filter. One LFO (triangle or square, 0.01 to 100 Hz) is normalled to both oscillators' pitch, with a switch to exempt VCO1. A noise generator, a two-input voltage processor with a normal and an inverted output, and 30 CV and audio patch points: almost every knob has a matching CV input, including both waveform controls and all six envelope stages.

modules.name: MIDI interface
modules.description: Converts MIDI notes to pitch and gate. There is no keyboard; notes arrive on the top-panel MIDI IN or over USB.

modules.name: Pitch and tune
modules.description: Combines the MIDI pitch with the external 1 V/octave CV IN and the master tune, and feeds both oscillators and the filter's keyboard tracking.

modules.name: Gate routing
modules.description: Delivers the gate that fires both envelopes. MIDI note gate by default; the GATE IN jack substitutes an external gate, for example from an analogue sequencer. Polarity can be inverted in SynthTRIBE. The GATE LED shows it.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Triangle or square, 0.01 to 100 Hz, with a rate CV input. One output is scaled by the LFO VOLUME knob, the other is unattenuated. The scaled output is normalled to the oscillators' modulation input.

modules.name: VCO modulation routing
modules.description: Distributes the pitch modulation (the LFO via LFO VOLUME unless VCO MOD IN is patched) to both oscillators, with VCO 1 MOD OFF removing VCO1 from it. Also holds the switch that picks the pulse-width modulation source.

modules.name: VCO 1
modules.description: Analogue VCO whose single WAVEFORM control morphs continuously from triangle through ramp and sawtooth to square and pulse; at fully clockwise the pulse width follows the selected PWM source. Frequency, waveform and level each have a CV input.

frequency_hz.note: panel scale, 440 Hz at centre; the guide says plus or minus 2 octaves

modules.name: VCO 1 VCA
modules.description: Level control for VCO 1 before the filter, set by its VOLUME knob and a CV input. This is how the two oscillators are mixed, and why the mix can be voltage controlled.

modules.name: VCO 2
modules.description: Analogue VCO whose single WAVEFORM control morphs continuously from triangle through ramp and sawtooth to square and pulse; at fully clockwise the pulse width follows the selected PWM source. Frequency, waveform and level each have a CV input. Can be hard-synced to VCO1, and has the fine BEAT control against it.

frequency_hz.note: panel scale, 440 Hz at centre; the guide says plus or minus 2 octaves

modules.name: VCO 2 VCA
modules.description: Level control for VCO 2 before the filter, set by its VOLUME knob and a CV input. This is how the two oscillators are mixed, and why the mix can be voltage controlled.

modules.name: VCF
modules.description: 24 dB/octave low-pass filter. Self-oscillates at the top of the resonance range. Keyboard tracking from 0 to 200%, envelope depth from ADS 2, and CV inputs for frequency, resonance and envelope depth. Takes both VCO VCAs and an external audio input.

modules.name: ADS 1
modules.description: Attack, decay and sustain envelope driving the output VCA. There is no release control: DECAY sets both the decay and the release time. Every stage has its own CV input. DECAY OFF forces decay and release to zero.

modules.name: ADS 2
modules.description: Attack, decay and sustain envelope driving the filter. There is no release control: DECAY sets both the decay and the release time. Every stage has its own CV input.

modules.name: Output VCA
modules.description: Amplifier after the filter, opened by ADS 1.

modules.name: Noise generator
modules.description: White or pink noise, patch-only: the panel draws its line to the NOISE OUT jack and nowhere else.

modules.name: Voltage processor
modules.description: Two-input voltage processor. Input 1 carries +10 V DC unless something is patched, scaled by IN 1 GAIN; input 2 has a fixed gain of 2. The sum is scaled by OUT GAIN and available normal and inverted. With nothing patched it is a manual offset voltage source.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Master volume feeding the 3.5 mm front and 6.35 mm rear audio outputs and the headphone socket.

behaviours.name: Morphing waveforms
behaviours.rule: Each VCO has one WAVEFORM knob and one waveform CV input that sweep continuously through triangle, ramp, sawtooth, square and pulse. Intermediate positions are valid timbres, not detents. At fully clockwise the pulse width is modulated by the source chosen on the LFO/BOTH/ADS switch.

behaviours.name: Per-oscillator VCAs
behaviours.rule: Each VCO has its own VCA before the filter, set by its VOLUME knob and a CV input. The oscillator mix is therefore voltage controllable: an envelope or LFO into VCO 1 VOLUME and VCO 2 VOLUME crossfades them.

behaviours.name: Pitch modulation normal
behaviours.rule: The LFO, scaled by LFO VOLUME, is normalled to both VCOs' modulation input. VCO MOD IN replaces it. VCO 1 MOD OFF exempts VCO1, which with SYNCHRO on gives sync sweeps with a stable fundamental.

behaviours.name: Asymmetric VCO outputs
behaviours.rule: VCO 1 OUT is a tap; VCO1 still feeds the filter. VCO 2 OUT is a TRS insert: a mono plug takes VCO2 out and cuts it from the filter; a Y-cable (tip send, ring return) lets VCO2 be processed externally and returned.

behaviours.name: ADS envelopes
behaviours.rule: Both envelopes are attack, decay, sustain; DECAY also sets the release, as on a Minimoog. DECAY OFF on the VCA envelope zeroes decay and release for an organ-style gate. The gate input description calls them ASR.

behaviours.name: Voltage processor
behaviours.rule: Out = OUT GAIN x (IN 1 GAIN x in1 + 2 x in2), with REV OUT its inverse. With nothing patched, in1 is +10 V, so OUT and REV OUT are manual positive and negative offsets. Gains are marked 0 to 2 on the panel.

behaviours.name: Everything is voltage controllable
behaviours.rule: Almost every knob has a matching CV input: VCO frequency, waveform and level, filter frequency, resonance and envelope depth, every envelope stage, LFO rate. The guide suggests external modulation sources such as the Behringer Abacus. Whether each input sums with its knob or replaces it is not stated; sum is assumed.

behaviours.name: Self-oscillating filter
behaviours.rule: The filter self-oscillates at the top of the resonance range. With KEYB CTRL at 100% (1 V/octave) it tracks pitch as a sine source. KEYB CTRL goes to 200%.

behaviours.name: Refiltering and fuzz
behaviours.rule: The guide suggests feeding one of the Expander's own outputs back into VCF AUDIO IN to refilter, and overdriving that input for fuzz before the filter.

note_to_cv.scaling: 1 V/octave (CV IN is 1 V/octave; MIDI is assumed to match)

source_inconsistencies: The LFO waveform switch (29) offers triangle and square; the specifications list square, S&H and triangle.
DECAY OFF (33) acts on the VCA envelope, which is ADS 1; the specifications call it ADS 2 Decay Off.
GATE IN (11) calls the envelopes ASR; everywhere else they are ADS.
VCO FREQUENCY (20) is described as plus or minus 2 octaves; the panel scale runs 10 Hz to 10 kHz, about ten octaves.
USB (64) is type B in the controls list and USB Micro in the specifications.
The specifications describe a top-panel slider power switch and a rear push button; the controls list has one POWER SWITCH.
LFO OUTPUT 2 is printed as 'LFO OUTPUT 1' in the Chinese section.

modelling_gaps.detail: None given anywhere; the knobs are marked 1 to 10.
The order of shapes is stated; where each shape sits on the knob, and what the in-between shapes are, is not.
Self-oscillation is stated; resonance law, cutoff taper and filter topology are not.
Only CV IN (1 V/octave) and KEYB CTRL (0 to 2 V/octave) have stated scaling. No input voltage ranges are given for any other jack.
No RSF Kobol documentation was supplied; it would be the source for ranges and the waveform morph.
